title: CUDA SSD-streaming machinery proven on DSV4 weights (upstream ds4 master)
capture_method: single scripted run as dsv4 (g1_smoke.sh via 'sudo -u dsv4 bash -s'); raw logs copied verbatim into results/glm52-gates/logs/g1/. A first run at 11:47 passed 11/12 with the only FAIL being a harness race (ready-file read before memwatch's first 2-s poll cycle; memwatch.log proved ARMED 1 s after server start). The harness wait was fixed to wait for ARMED content and the ENTIRE run was re-executed cleanly at 11:49 — the committed evidence is the full 11:49 rerun, not a patched first run.

raw_logs.note: server.log filtered only of per-token load-progress and per-request kv-trace spam lines (filter recorded in repo history); all startup/streaming/shutdown lines intact. run1.json/run2.json are the raw HTTP bodies; run1.text/run2.text the extracted completions (159 bytes each).

assertions_summary.name: memwatch_armed
assertions_summary.actual: ARMED 96439 96422 70210224 engine (pid verified child-of-sudo-wrapper; identity ticks checked by 01_memwatch.sh itself)

assertions_summary.name: server_ready
assertions_summary.actual: /v1/models 200 after ~5 s (streaming: only 0.99 GiB token-embedding span mapped at startup)

assertions_summary.name: byte_identical
assertions_summary.expected: temp-0 seed-42 fixed prompt, extracted text bytes equal across two consecutive requests

assertions_summary.name: read_bytes_growth_run1
assertions_summary.expected: >= 2 GiB via /proc/<pid>/io during completion (O_DIRECT streamed expert reads are page-cache-invisible, so read_bytes is disk-real)

assertions_summary.name: streaming_engaged
assertions_summary.actual: 'cuda SSD streaming total expert budget 16.00 GiB = 3.38 GiB prefill headroom + 12.62 GiB dynamic cache (1915 experts, 6.75 MiB each)' + 'SSD streaming initial cuda model map restricted to token embedding'

assertions_summary.name: memwatch_no_breach
assertions_summary.actual: 0 breach lines; min sampled MemAvailable 86.72 GiB vs 10 GiB line; ARMED->DISARMED bracket clean

recorded_not_gated.observation: run2 re-read 83.9 GB vs run1's 84.6 GB — the 12.62 GiB dynamic cache yields ~1% reuse across identical consecutive requests on the 61-layer DSV4 path. This is the sol-predicted near-zero-hit CUDA behavior and is exactly what G4a (persistent CUDA expert cache) exists to fix.
recorded_not_gated.effective_read_throughput: ~3.3 GB/s during decode vs 10.7 GB/s sequential NVMe — selected-expert reads do not reach sequential bandwidth, as predicted.

waivers.criterion: prod stopped for a bounded window, then restored and verified (tailnet 401 + warm probe < 2 s)
waivers.reasoning: Prod was found already down before G1 began: ds4 v0.4.2 received a clean 'shutdown requested' 2026-07-23 21:34 EDT (ds4-server.log) with a clean memwatch DISARM; a llama.cpp engine then served until a clean 'cleaning up before exit' 2026-07-24 09:36 EDT. No crash, no OOM (journal clean), no reboot (uptime 8 days). The user directive for this work authorizes keeping DeepSeek down until GLM is verified ('you may shut down the current deepseek model running/do whatever else you need'). Auth chain verified untouched during G1: dsv4-authhelper + caddy active, tailnet-facing :8010 returns 401. Full DSV4 restore + warm-probe verification is deferred to G5, whose round-trip gate proves it end-to-end.
